chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Riab, from Durays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The slave, when he confesses once before the Imam that he has stolen, his hand is cut, and the slave girl, when she confesses upon herself regarding the theft, her hand is cut.

key_terms.الْإِمَام: The Imam (ruler/judge) before whom the confession is made
key_terms.قَطَعَ: He cut (referring to the amputation of the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the requirement for cutting the hand of a slave who confesses to theft?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'iqrar' (self-confession) as a standalone proof for the hadd of theft, emphasizing the Imam's authority to execute the penalty based on the thief's own admission. It specifically notes that a single confession suffices for both male and female slaves, reflecting the juristic view that their testimony or confession carries weight in establishing the crime without requiring additional witnesses. This ruling underscores the procedural efficiency in Shia jurisprudence where the accused's own words serve as the primary evidence for applying the fixed punishment.
